h: Humility Heals the Pride That Obstructs Holy Delight

p: are in the secret of ONeG,
the initials of Eden, Nahar, Gan
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בְּרֵאשִׁית כו, א)
(as is written in the holy Zohar, Bereishis, I 26a);
and whoever does not fulfill them
while he has the means to fulfill them,
it is turned into a nega of tzaraas
from the Ra'aya Mehemna and the Tikkunim).
And it appears that this is also alluded to
אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מֵשִׂים לִבּוֹ כְּבָשָׂר
unless he makes his heart like flesh,
'And it shall be, from new moon to new moon
Regarding 'flesh' it is written 'and it is healed';
regarding 'man' it is not written 'and it is healed.'"
And in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Metzora 3) it is stated:
"And because he raised himself up like a cedar,
therefore he is healed through hyssop."
וְחָשַׁב עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְגִלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת בֵּינֵיהֶם
and it counts idolatry and forbidden relations among them;
and in the Gemara it counts among the seven things
That is, the roots of the kelipos are seven,
corresponding to the seven lower traits in holiness
"God made the one opposite the other" (Koheles 7:14);
and when each is comprised of ten, they are seventy;
and corresponding to them are the seven nations,
and their root is the Kenaani, the Chitti and the Emori;
and they correspond to the heads of the kelipos,
which are jealousy, desire and honor;
and these are opposite the holiness of the Avos,
who are the opposite of these three traits.
is the opposite of the kelipah of jealousy,
which is the kelipah of Esav,
שֶׁהוּא שׂוֹנֵא דָּמוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם בְּגוּפוֹ
who hates the blood of a person within his body,
whose trait was dread and fear,
is the opposite of the kelipah of desire,
who was lowly in his own eyes
and said "I am too small, etc.,"
is opposite the kelipah of pride and honor,
which is the kelipah of Amalek,
as is stated in the Midrash
"'A man's pride will bring him low' (Mishlei 29:23)
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing,
(in his sefer, parshas Lech Lecha), reckoned:
corresponds to the trait of chessed in holiness;
the Chitti, from the word chatas, dread,
corresponds to the trait of fear in holiness;
corresponds to the trait of tiferes in holiness,
and these are the three traits
for which the Avos are a chariot.
which are the opposite of the life
of the holiness of the Avos.
corresponds to the kelipah of Yishmael,
which is the dross of the trait of chessed
and the Chitti corresponds to the kelipah of Esav, jealousy,
which is the dross of the trait of gevurah
and the Emori corresponds to pride,
"Yet I destroyed the Emori before them,
whose height was like the height of cedars."
branch out the three grave sins,
עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים
and the root of pride is
"I will ascend above the heights of the clouds,
I will be like the Most High" (Yeshayahu 14:14);
וְהוּא רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק (בְּמִדְבַּר כד, כ)
and that is "Amalek, the first of the nations" (Bamidbar 24:20),
which is the head of the roots of the kelipos.
And the beginning of the serpent's incitement
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁלָּבַשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
And because HaKadosh Baruch Hu put on
that His kingship, may He be blessed, be revealed,
"Hashem reigns, He is garbed in grandeur"
from this there branched out, in the reverse, the pride
in the world that was destroyed,
of which it is written "and he reigned and he died"
and that is the kelipah of idolatry.
And through it the nega'im come,
that he raised himself up like a cedar.
And the Gemara concludes (there, and in the Tanchuma):
for so you find with Uziyahu (Divrei HaYamim II 26:16, 19):
וּבְחֶזְקָתוֹ גָּבַהּ לִבּוֹ עַד לְהַשְׁחִית וְגוֹ׳
"And when he was strong, his heart grew haughty to his ruin, etc.,
to burn incense upon the altar of incense, etc.;
and in his rage with the kohanim,
the tzaraas shone forth on his forehead, etc."
That is, the matter of the incense
so that even the galbanum gives a good fragrance;
and it alludes to the transgressors of Yisrael
That is, that even the transgressors of Yisrael
are destined to give a good fragrance."
And this power was given over to Aharon
and to his descendants after him.
And Uziyahu was very great in stature,
and he thought that he was
greater in stature than the kohanim,
and that it was in his power to burn incense
that the transgressors of Yisrael give a good fragrance.
is needed for the service of Hashem Yisbarach,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב יז, ו)
"And his heart was lifted up in the ways of Hashem."
That is, the yetzer hara entices a person
"What is his strength and his understanding,
and what will he accomplish with his deeds?"
And a person must lift up his heart
and know that through his deeds
he effects rectification above, in the supernal root,
as is written in the holy Zohar
"The Rock who bore you, you weaken"
that they weaken the power above
אַךְ הוּא צְרִיכָה לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
But it is needed for the service of Hashem Yisbarach,
"And his heart was lifted up in the ways of Hashem."
But one must be very careful
שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא עַל יְדֵי זֶה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
that he not come through this, Heaven forbid,
"And when he was strong, his heart grew haughty to his ruin":
for through pride in his own stature
one can come to the lowest depths;
"and in his rage with the kohanim,
the tzaraas shone forth on his forehead"
for to this the forehead points,
"'And the light' — this is the forehead, etc."
And this is the root of the yetzer hara:
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא סוֹטָה הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
And this is what they said in the Gemara, Sotah, cited above:
"Regarding 'flesh' it is written 'and it is healed'":
that is, whoever is like flesh,
of him is written immediately "and it is healed";
"and it is healed" is not written next to it;
rather he needs to be healed
And the holiness of the new month
which has nothing of its own;
from the light of the sun,
and it signifies humility and lowliness.
"And where is the place of My rest?"
and it is written after it (66:2):
"But to this one will I look,
to the poor and broken of spirit, etc."
when dread and fear fall upon a person,
he becomes poor and broken of spirit,
all that has passed over him,
"And it shall be, from new moon to new moon
all flesh shall come to bow down, etc.,"
because then he grasps his own lowliness;
and that is the opposite of nega,
for of "flesh" it is written "and it is healed."
But one who is the opposite of this,
and is proud like a cedar,
and considers himself in the category of "man"
of him "and it is healed" is not written,
until he lowers himself like hyssop.
And this is what they said in the Gemara:
אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מֵשִׂים לִבּוֹ כְּבָשָׂר
"unless he makes his heart like flesh."
וּבִפְרָט כְּשֶׁהוּא שַׁבָּת וְרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ בְּיַחַד
And especially when it is Shabbos and Rosh Chodesh together,
the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
which is the opposite of pride;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לְהִתְעַנֵּג בְּעֹנֶג
and through this one merits to delight in oneg.
he is granted the requests of his heart,
